title: Sovereign Citizen Claims He Has NO NAME... Judge Wolfe OBLITERATES Him!

vo.text: This man walked into court on his own criminal case and told the judge he doesn't have a name. He says he's not the defendant. He's the attorney of fact for the defendant. No law license, no power of attorney, just a stack of sovereign citizen paperwork. Judge Wolfe gave him every chance to stop the nonsense. What happened next is one of the cleanest shutdowns you'll ever see. Let's get into it.

So here's the game. Matthew Aldridge is charged in a criminal case, and his trial is set for tomorrow. But instead of saying yes, I'm Matthew Aldridge, he calls himself the attorney of fact. In sovereign citizen land, that's supposed to separate the man from the legal name on the case, so the court supposedly can't touch him. And when the judge asks his name, he says he doesn't have one. Judge Wolfe has clearly seen this before. Watch how calm he stays.

And there it is. Only a licensed attorney can represent a criminal defendant in Tennessee. Not an attorney of fact, not a friend, not a version of yourself. Judge Wolfe even gave him an out. Do you have a power of attorney? No. So he has zero authority to speak for Matthew Aldridge. But he didn't come empty handed. He brought paperwork. And Judge Wolfe is about to read it out loud, word for word, in open court.

Let's break down what he just filed. He's demanding that the State of Tennessee prove its standing against a man, citing an eighteen hundreds civil case about a canal company and some Latin phrases. He gives the court fifteen days to prove itself, or he says it has to cease and desist. None of that applies to a criminal case. It's copy and paste sovereign citizen material. And the judge is about to explain exactly why it means nothing.

That is how you shut it down. Judge Wolfe tells him the court's power comes from the United States Constitution, the Tennessee Constitution, and the voters of Cheatham County, not from his paperwork. Notice he never raises his voice. He just keeps putting the facts on the record. And instead of taking the hint, this guy tries one more line. He asks if the trial will be free. Judge Wolfe's answer is perfect.

And that's the end of the attorney of fact. The so called filing was denied because it doesn't cite a single valid criminal statute. The trial is set for July fifteenth, the last plea day is July eighth, and if Matthew Aldridge doesn't show up, his bond gets revoked and he goes to trial from jail. He came to fight the court's jurisdiction and walked out with a court card and a deadline. Do you think he shows up on July eighth? Let me know in the comments.
